explain.say: Electricity is sold in kilowatt-hours, often just called units. One kilowatt-hour is the energy used by something with a power of 1,000 watts running for one hour, which is 3.6 million joules.

faq.a: It is a unit of energy: the energy used by a 1,000 watt appliance running for one hour. It equals 3.6 million joules, and it is the unit on electricity bills, often called a unit.
asks: What is a unit of electricity?

faq.q: What is the difference between a joule and a kilowatt-hour?
faq.a: Both measure energy. A joule is tiny, about the energy needed to lift an apple one metre, so for electricity we use kilowatt-hours: one kilowatt-hour is 3.6 million joules.
asks: How many joules in a kilowatt-hour?

faq.q: How do you work out how many kilowatt-hours something uses?
faq.a: Multiply its power in kilowatts by how many hours it runs. A 100 watt TV, which is 0.1 kilowatts, running for 5 hours uses 0.5 kilowatt-hours.
asks: How do I calculate energy use?

faq.q: How much energy does boiling a kettle use?
faq.a: Heating one litre of water from the tap to boiling takes about 0.1 kilowatt-hours. Boiling only the water you need saves energy.
asks: Does boiling a kettle use a lot of electricity?

faq.q: Why does an electric shower use so much energy?
faq.a: Heating water takes a lot of energy, and an electric shower heats it instantly as it flows, so it needs about 8 to 10 kilowatts. Ten minutes uses about 1.5 kilowatt-hours.
asks: How much does a shower cost to run?

facts: A typical British home uses roughly 2,700 kilowatt-hours of electricity a year.

quiz.say: A 2 kilowatt heater runs for 3 hours. How much energy does it use?
quiz.why: Energy is power times time: 2 kilowatts times 3 hours is 6 kilowatt-hours.

wrong.1: 1.5 comes from dividing 3 by 2; you multiply power by time.
wrong.2: 5 comes from adding; you multiply power by time.
